title: Clair Road West housing and employment land conversion
subtitle: College Avenue apartments, Arkell Road and 132 Clair Road West subdivisions, Ward heritage district, livestream outage
overview: Council approved an Official Plan and zoning change for 266 and 280 Clair Road West and part of 950 Southgate Drive, converting industrial land to high-density housing {{vote:m9}}. Staff had recommended refusal because the employment land conversion was not justified, and council instead used staff's alternative conditions. Council also asked staff to study a CMHC income-based definition of affordability for the project and report back by the first quarter of 2027.

Council approved a seven-storey apartment building at 210, 214 and 222 College Avenue East {{vote:m10}}. It approved a subdivision at 220 Arkell Road, with a direction to leave neighbouring street addresses out of the draft plan conditions, and a subdivision with rezoning at 132 Clair Road West. On the consent agenda, council designated the Ward Heritage Conservation District, approved a heritage permit for towers at 55 Baker Street and authorized notice to designate 35 McTague Street.

Before the open meeting, council met in closed session on Comprehensive Zoning By-law appeals at the Ontario Land Tribunal and gave direction to staff. No further detail was reported. The livestream failed during the meeting, but council continued because the meeting was being recorded.

decisions.item: Clair Road West and Southgate Drive redesignation and rezoning
decisions.detail: Council approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments for high-density residential use on former industrial land, following staff's alternative conditions rather than the staff refusal {{vote:m9}}.

Notwithstanding the affordable housing commitment in the conditions, staff will evaluate the CMHC income-based affordability definition for the Clair Road development and report back by Q1 2027 {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments to allow a seven-storey, 117-unit purpose-built apartment building on lands now designated low density {{vote:m10}}.

Council approved the rezoning and a three-year draft plan of subdivision with 32 detached lots and a townhouse block, and directed staff to omit adjacent property addresses from the conditions {{vote:m14}}.
Council approved Official Plan and zoning amendments and a three-year draft plan of subdivision for Mattamy's low-density and multiple residential blocks {{vote:m15}}.
Council designated the Ward Heritage Conservation District by by-law and adopted its district plan under the Ontario Heritage Act.
Council approved heritage permit HP26-0002 for the North and South Towers at 55 Baker Street, including 152 and 160 Wyndham Street North.

debate: On Clair Road West, staff said the employment land conversion was not justified, noise from neighbouring industry could not be ruled out as a concern, and the ecological linkage and stormwater design had unresolved issues. Staff said the site is a viable employment size and cited smaller sites that hold hundreds of jobs.

The applicant team argued the site is constrained, that the city would keep enough employment land, and that the project would deliver ownership housing for local workers. A consultant said noise and air studies showed compatibility, with a Class 4 noise designation, warning clauses and air conditioning. A delegate opposed to the project raised air quality, noise, limited green space and stormwater flooding onto the replacement ecological linkage.

Councillors questioned how owner-occupancy and long-term affordability would be kept without title restrictions. Finance staff noted that nonprofit development charge exemptions cannot be tied to affordability and that the city's development charge reserves are already overcommitted. Several councillors said they wanted to reach a yes, but worried that fixed conditions could make the project unviable.

On College Avenue East, the adjacent homeowner and a neighbouring golf club objected to the building's scale, shadows on the golf course, parking overflow and trespass. The applicant and the golf club's planner accepted staff's recommended limits, including seven storeys and higher parking. The applicant asked to remove the holding provisions, and staff said they were needed to confirm services before zoning proceeds. Three councillors voted against, citing massing and the building's likely student use.

At Arkell Road, a neighbouring landowner raised fencing, trespass and the naming of an adjacent address in the conditions. The applicant offered to add no-trespassing signage, and council removed specific addresses from the conditions.
